## How Transcat Biomed Supports the Plasma Supply Chain


The demand for plasma-derived therapies continues to rise, creating new opportunities and challenges for plasma collection organizations. As healthcare providers treat more patients with immune deficiencies, bleeding disorders, neurological conditions, liver disease, and other chronic illnesses, the need for a reliable plasma supply has **never been greater** .


Meeting that demand requires more than opening additional donation centers. Every new facility must be equipped to safely collect, freeze, store, monitor, and transport plasma while complying with strict regulatory requirements. For operators expanding their networks, the challenge isn't simply increasing capacity. It's ensuring every location can deliver consistent performance from day one.


That's where the right combination of equipment qualification, calibration, environmental monitoring, and ongoing compliance support becomes critical.


## Strict Regulations


When people think about plasma collection, they often focus on the donation process itself. But the work of protecting plasma begins long before it reaches a manufacturer and continues throughout every stage of storage and handling.


Temperature control is one of the most important variables in the process. Plasma products must be frozen, monitored, and maintained within tightly controlled conditions to preserve their quality and suitability for use in life-saving therapies. Even a single storage excursion can create significant operational and compliance concerns.


As plasma collection organizations grow, maintaining those standards across multiple locations becomes increasingly difficult. New facilities need to be brought online quickly. Equipment must be qualified before use. Documentation needs to support inspections and audits. At the same time, operations teams are focused on opening doors, training staff, and meeting collection targets.


The pressure to move quickly can never come at the expense of compliance.


## Expansion Creates New Operational Challenges


For many plasma collection organizations, expansion is occurring at a rapid pace.


Opening a new center involves much more than installing freezers and connecting monitoring systems. Organizations must demonstrate that critical storage equipment has been installed correctly, operates as intended, and consistently performs under real-world conditions.


This process, known as equipment qualification, creates documented evidence that systems are ready for use. It also helps organizations identify and address potential issues before they affect operations.


Without a well-planned qualification strategy, equipment validation activities can quickly become a bottleneck. Opening schedules are delayed, inspections become more stressful, and internal teams are stretched thin managing documentation and testing requirements.


The challenge becomes even greater when multiple facilities are launching simultaneously.


## Case Study: Supporting Seven New Plasma Donation Centers


A recent Transcat Biomed project illustrates how these challenges play out in practice.


A regional plasma collection organization was preparing to open seven new donation centers. Each facility required plasma freezers capable of maintaining stringent storage conditions, and each freezer needed to be fully qualified before the centers could begin operations and prepare for regulatory inspections.


The timeline was aggressive. The qualification work needed to be completed without slowing facility openings or disrupting broader expansion plans.


To support the project, Transcat Biomed executed a comprehensive Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), and Performance Qualification (PQ) program across all seven sites.


The effort began with installation verification, equipment identification reviews, mechanical inspections, calibration assessments, and environmental evaluations. Once installation requirements were confirmed, teams validated freezer controls, alarm functionality, monitoring systems, and operating parameters.


The most extensive testing occurred during Performance Qualification activities. Temperature mapping studies evaluated freezer performance both empty and loaded at -40°C. Daily packing simulations and shipping movement studies replicated real operating conditions, while freeze studies verified that plasma products could consistently reach required temperatures within established timeframes.


The result was a complete body of documented evidence demonstrating that the equipment was properly installed, operating as intended, and capable of maintaining performance under actual use conditions.


## Qualification Is Only the Beginning


While qualification is an important milestone, maintaining compliant plasma storage requires an ongoing commitment to equipment performance.


Temperature sensors drift over time. Monitoring systems require calibration. Alarms need verification. Preventive maintenance schedules must be followed. Documentation needs to remain organized and accessible.


Successful plasma storage programs are built around a lifecycle approach that combines qualification, calibration, maintenance, and compliance management into a single strategy.


This is where many organizations see value in working with a partner that can support the entire process rather than individual projects.


## Building Long-Term Confidence in Plasma Storage


Transcat Biomed supports blood and plasma organizations through services that extend well beyond initial freezer qualification.


Calibration programs help ensure temperature sensors, monitoring equipment, and environmental systems continue delivering accurate data. Preventive maintenance services reduce downtime and help organizations identify potential issues before they become operational problems. Documentation management and electronic validation platforms help simplify audit readiness and strengthen data integrity.


For organizations operating multiple facilities, these services create consistency across locations while reducing the burden on internal teams.


More importantly, they help ensure that plasma products remain protected throughout the storage lifecycle.


## Supporting Every Step of the Plasma Journey


The growing demand for plasma-derived therapies shows no signs of slowing. As collection organizations continue expanding to serve more patients, the need for reliable storage systems, documented compliance, and dependable operational support will only increase.


Safe plasma storage starts with qualified equipment, but it doesn't end there. It requires ongoing calibration, performance verification, preventive maintenance, and a commitment to continuous compliance.


Through a combination of qualification, temperature mapping, calibration, maintenance, and operational support, Transcat Biomed helps plasma collection organizations build and maintain the infrastructure required to support a safe and reliable plasma supply chain.


The seven-site qualification project is just one real-world example of how the right support can help organizations expand confidently while maintaining the standards that regulators, patients, and healthcare providers depend on.
